$comment: Machine-readable claims for the Uncloud family-homes validator. Built by build-claims.cjs from CAMPAIGN.md/COPY.md (CI-Common, read 2026-10-01), the voice canon and cross-checks against code. Validator contract in STORY-BIBLE.md section 13.

validator.appliesTo: every user-facing string: titles, headings, popups, captions, narration scripts, alt text, aria-labels, og/meta tags, share pages, README for the site. Skip code identifiers, URLs, file names and JSON keys.

severity.review: fail unless the exact string is on the reviewed allow-list with an owner initial

validator.flags: Patterns are JS RegExp sources; use the given flags. Strip HTML tags first. Normalise curly quotes.
validator.disclosureCheck: For each disclosure with required:true, the page/film must contain its text (or the long form with the family name) in the place listed under where.
validator.appCheck: Every Hub app named in a story must match apps[].display or storeName (case-insensitive) and the story must stay inside mayDescribeAs and caveats. Unknown app names fail.

sourceTags.hold: conflicted or unsigned: do not print until the owner rules

sources: CI-OS core/headless (setup hotspot); CI-Docs getting-started and portal pages

bannedPhrases.why: Voice rule: never an em or en dash in user-facing copy. Use a comma, semicolon or period.
bannedPhrases.fix: Rewrite with a comma, semicolon or full stop.

bannedPhrases.why: A typed double hyphen is an em dash in disguise.
bannedPhrases.fix: Use a comma or a period.

bannedPhrases.why: A spaced hyphen reads as a dash.
bannedPhrases.fix: Use a comma or a period.

bannedPhrases.why: MESSAGING.md: no exclamation marks. Success is grounded, not gushing.
bannedPhrases.fix: End with a full stop.

bannedPhrases.why: No emoji in product copy.
bannedPhrases.fix: Remove.

bannedPhrases.why: Trailing ellipsis is suspense, not the Uncloud voice.
bannedPhrases.fix: Finish the sentence.

bannedPhrases.why: Banned buzzword list (brand-voice.md Part I, uncloud-voice SKILL, COPY.md section 0, MESSAGING.md).
bannedPhrases.fix: Name the fact instead of the adjective.

bannedPhrases.why: "AI-powered solution" is the corporate SaaS framing CI opposes.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say what the agent does.

bannedPhrases.why: Platitude. This stack is not for everyone and saying so is a landmine.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say who it is for: individuals, families and small teams who want powerful AI without cloud dependency.

bannedPhrases.why: Vocabulary: "no rate limits", not "unlimited" (sounds like a SaaS upsell).
bannedPhrases.fix: Say "no rate limits" only where the sheet allows it, or name the fact.

bannedPhrases.why: Ease claims are unmeasured. The only sanctioned ease line is "Plug it in, pair it over Wi-Fi, and walk away."
bannedPhrases.fix: Show the steps instead of calling them easy.

bannedPhrases.why: Vocabulary: "sign in", not "log in".
bannedPhrases.fix: Sign in / sign out.

bannedPhrases.why: Vocabulary: OpenClaw and Hermes are agents, never chatbots.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say agent, or name OpenClaw or Hermes.

bannedPhrases.why: Vocabulary: agent, not assistant. (Marketplace manifests say "assistant"; our copy does not.)
bannedPhrases.fix: Say agent.

bannedPhrases.why: Vocabulary: say Companion Core, not home server, NAS, box or appliance.
bannedPhrases.fix: Companion Core, or "your Core" after first mention.

bannedPhrases.why: "Box" is allowed only to mean the Core ("One box. No subscription.").
bannedPhrases.fix: Say your Core.

bannedPhrases.why: Vocabulary: "the Companion Hub store" (the sheet's phrase). Not app store or marketplace.
bannedPhrases.fix: the Companion Hub store.

bannedPhrases.why: Vocabulary: Companion Memory.
bannedPhrases.fix: Companion Memory.

bannedPhrases.why: The Kickstarter draft says Digital Memory; the product name is Companion Memory.
bannedPhrases.fix: Companion Memory.

bannedPhrases.why: User-facing name is "Companion account", never Portal or CI Account.
bannedPhrases.fix: Companion account.

bannedPhrases.why: Repo and wizard-label names are engineering surfaces. Use product names. (The Hub wizard labels Companion Memory "CI Memory"; do not copy that.)
bannedPhrases.fix: Companion Hub, Companion Memory, Companion OS.

bannedPhrases.why: Vocabulary: uncloud, local-first.
bannedPhrases.fix: uncloud / local-first.

bannedPhrases.why: Product nouns are Title Case: Companion Core, Companion Hub, Companion Memory, Companion OS. Only "account" stays lower case: Companion account.
bannedPhrases.fix: Capitalise the product noun.

bannedPhrases.why: "Companion account" has a lower-case a.
bannedPhrases.fix: Companion account.

bannedPhrases.why: Spell OpenClaw and Hermes exactly.
bannedPhrases.fix: OpenClaw, Hermes.

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(Companion Core Subscription|Core Subscription|Import Tools|Memory Import Tools|Companion Earth|Companion Atlas|Spatial Atlas)\b
bannedPhrases.why: Retired or mistitled names (CAMPAIGN.md 2c, PLATFORM-VISION cautions). Import is built into Companion Memory.
bannedPhrases.fix: Remove, or say Companion Memory imports your data.

bannedPhrases.why: Sign-off is exactly "UnCloud your life." with that capitalisation.
bannedPhrases.fix: UnCloud your life.

bannedPhrases.why: No prices anywhere on the site. The Kickstarter ladder was re-priced repeatedly between 8 and 23 Sep (CAMPAIGN.md 2b to 2e), the shop and the campaign disagree, and copy.json holds a third set. Link to the campaign page instead.
bannedPhrases.fix: Remove the number; link to the campaign page.

bannedPhrases.why: No savings or payback figures. They depend on the rented-stack table and its caveat; the sheet (about ten months) and copy.json (about 26 months) disagree; the 75% and 95% figures are marketing math.
bannedPhrases.fix: Describe the app, not the arithmetic.

bannedPhrases.why: No productivity or time-saved figure exists. "Get more done" must be shown as a concrete task, never as a number.
bannedPhrases.fix: Show the task the agent did.

bannedPhrases.why: Companion has published no tok/s for any model on any tier (CAMPAIGN.md 4). Geerling figures are third-party and not ours.
bannedPhrases.fix: Remove.

bannedPhrases.why: Only "19 dB at idle" is measured. An unqualified acoustic number is what Design and Technology review picks at.
bannedPhrases.fix: 19 dB at idle.

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(power draw|watts? (idle|typical|at load|peak)|electricity (cost|bill)|pennies a day|energy[- ]efficient|low[- ]power|sustained temperature|runs cool|stays cool|weighs?|(?<!open[- ])weight|\d+\s?(kg|lbs?|pounds)|operating temperature|input voltage|FCC|UKCA|CE[- ]marked|RoHS|WEEE|Energy Star|FlexATX|SFX|ROCm\s?\d|CUDA)\b
bannedPhrases.why: Not measured or not confirmed (CAMPAIGN.md 4, 6): power draw, load noise, temperature, weight, voltage, certifications, PSU form factor, ROCm version.
bannedPhrases.fix: Remove.

bannedPhrases.why: The Core has a Noctua fan. The measured fact is 19 dB at idle; there is no load figure.
bannedPhrases.fix: Quiet at idle: 19 dB at idle.

bannedPhrases.why: No frame-rate, fps or refresh figure exists for Steam Headless on a Core: it depends on the GPU the Core has, the game and the network, and Companion has published none (same footing as num-tokens).
bannedPhrases.fix: Say what the family plays and where it streams to, with no figure.

bannedPhrases.why: An unmeasured performance claim: streaming a game over the home network can lag. (A "zero latency" claim is already caught by num-tokens.)
bannedPhrases.fix: Leave performance out; say where the game runs.

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(?!300\+ apps and agents available in the Companion Hub store)\d[\d,]*\+?\s+(?:free\s+|one[- ]click\s+|open[- ]source\s+|self[- ]hosted\s+)*(apps?|agents?|integrations?|services|tools|plugins|connectors|models|importers)\b|\ball (of )?(the )?\d+\b|\bevery app\b|\bany app\b|\bthousands of apps\b
bannedPhrases.why: The only app count is "300+ apps and agents available in the Companion Hub store." (owner ruling 22 Sep 2026). 84 integrations, 250+, 200+, 1,296 and 814 are all banned (cautions: 84 has no source; 1,296 is a directory count).
bannedPhrases.fix: Use the sanctioned sentence or no number.

bannedPhrases.why: Founder-letter number, not yet on the fact sheet (COPY.md 12.9).
bannedPhrases.fix: Remove unless the owner adds it to the sheet.

bannedPhrases.why: No measured setup or install time exists. "Installs in minutes" is a house pitch line but not on the campaign sheet.
bannedPhrases.fix: Show the steps; give no duration.

bannedPhrases.why: Fabrication-guard model names (HUB-MODELS cautions).
bannedPhrases.fix: Do not name models in stories.

bannedPhrases.why: Campaign economics are not retail facts and moved weekly. Terms belong on the Kickstarter page. Stories name no tier, price, ship date, warranty or backer perk.
bannedPhrases.fix: Link to the campaign page.

bannedPhrases.why: A year of Hub Pro (Companion Memory included) ships with a Core and renewal exists after it. "No cloud, no telemetry, no subscription" is a verbatim hero line on the sheet; in a story it needs the qualifier. "No API bill" is the safe line.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say "no API bill".

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(unhackable|hack[- ]proof|unbreakable|impenetrable|bullet[- ]?proof|military[- ]grade|bank[- ]grade|zero[- ]knowledge|end[- ]to[- ]end encrypt\w*|fully encrypted|encrypted by default|100%\s+(secure|private|safe|protected)|completely\s+(secure|safe|private|protected)|totally (safe|secure|private)|perfectly (safe|secure|private)|total privacy|absolute privacy|guarantee[sd]?|guaranteed|can(not|'t) be (hacked|breached|accessed|seen|read)|nobody (can|will) (see|read|access|get)|no one (can|will) (see|read|access|get))\b
bannedPhrases.why: No security or privacy guarantee. The sheet supports "Full-disk encryption is supported. Your keys." (supported, not default) and "Local by default". Absolute wording needs legal review (MEMORY-PAGE cautions).
bannedPhrases.fix: State where the data sits, not that it is unbreakable.

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(nothing|never|no data)\s+(ever\s+)?(leaves?|leaving|goes? (out|online|to the cloud)|phones? home|reaches? the cloud)\b|\bnever phones? home\b|\bzero (cloud )?telemetry\b|\bno tracking\b|\bnever (sees|sees your) (your )?data\b|\b(?:your|their|his|her|the family.s) (?:code|repos?|questions?|prompts?|homework|essays?|files?|photos?|games?|data)\s+(?:does(?:n.t| not)|do(?:n.t| not)|will not|won.t|can(?:not|.t))\s+(?:leave|go (?:out|online)|reach(?:es)? the cloud)\b
bannedPhrases.why: Not supportable: Hub is Portal-connected by default, store browsing and installs use the internet, crash reporting has been opt-out (PLATFORM-VISION cautions). The sheet's FAQ line is narrower: "No usage data is collected from your machine."
bannedPhrases.fix: Say "stays on your Core by default" or the FAQ line.

bannedPhrases.why: The Companion Hub store, app installs, the alternatives view and any messaging or web agent need the internet. The sheet claims only that no internet connection is required to use the machine you bought.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say which step uses the internet.

bannedPhrases.why: No compliance, certification or audit claim is supportable. OpenEMR in the catalogue is not HIPAA; Plausible's own listing says "GDPR" and we do not repeat it.
bannedPhrases.fix: Remove.

bannedPhrases.why: No medical claim. Fitness and recipe apps are record-keeping apps.
bannedPhrases.fix: Describe record-keeping only.

bannedPhrases.why: No safety guarantee. Pi-hole blocks ad and tracker domains; it is not parental control. Frigate records and detects objects; it does not guarantee a break-in is caught.
bannedPhrases.fix: Describe what the app records or blocks, in its own terms.

bannedPhrases.why: No legal, tax or financial claim. DocuSeal and Documenso sign documents; whether a signature is valid is not our statement.
bannedPhrases.fix: Describe the document workflow only.

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(you (could|may|might) be (hacked|spied|at risk|exposed)|hackers?|stalk\w*|predators?|identity theft|data breach(es)?|before it'?s too late|they are watching|watching you|spying|spies on|danger(ous)?|terrif\w+|scary|nightmare|panic|victims?)\b
bannedPhrases.why: Empower, do not frighten. Name the mechanism calmly; do not threaten the reader or show a family in danger.
bannedPhrases.fix: State the mechanism as a fact (where the data sits) and what the reader can do.

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(Google|Alphabet|Amazon|Alexa|Ring|Apple|iCloud|Siri|Meta|Facebook|Instagram|WhatsApp|Microsoft|OpenAI|ChatGPT|Anthropic|Zoom|Dropbox|Slack|Spotify|Netflix|Nest|Samsung|Adobe|Notion|Evernote|LastPass|1Password|Salesforce|Shopify|Mailchimp|GeForce Now|Xbox Cloud|Stadia)\b.{0,70}\b(spies?|spying|steals?|stole|sells? (your|the) data|selling (your|the) data|harvests?|mines? your|snoops?|exploits?|listens? (to|in on)|watching you|stalks?|lies|lying|abuses?|scams?|extorts?|holds? (you|your \w+) hostage|train(s|ed|ing)? (on|its models on) your)\b
bannedPhrases.why: No unsourced factual claim about a named company. The CI-Common matrix of such judgements is uncited. A Kickstarter-adjacent page is commercial speech; escalate comparative use to counsel.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say what the catalogue app does. Name the service only in the comparative form "<App> is an alternative to <Service>" (the second chip of a pair reads "alternative to <Service>"), and never in a sentence that says what the company does to you.

bannedPhrases.why: The logo of a service the Core replaces (Google, Apple, Amazon, Microsoft and the like) is never shown in authored text (CAMPAIGN.md 6c). An app's own real logo stands beside its name.
bannedPhrases.fix: Name the service in text.
bannedPhrases.scope: Authored text always. In page output an under portal/services/ is allowed only for a service whose registry mark (content/story/services.json) has mode logo, logoAllowed and cleared set by the owner, together with the names-logos-owners disclosure; the page test applies that exception, this pattern does not.

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(as (smart|good|capable|powerful|fast) as|on par with|matches|equals?|beats|outperforms?|better than|faster than|smarter than|replaces?|rival[sd]?|competes? with|frontier|state[- ]of[- ]the[- ]art model)\b.{0,50}\b(ChatGPT|GPT\S*|Claude|Gemini|OpenAI|Anthropic|cloud AI|the cloud|frontier|Copilot|Siri|Alexa)\b|\b(ChatGPT|GPT\S*|Claude|Gemini|OpenAI|Copilot)[- ](level|grade|class|quality|like|smart|good)\b|\bas (smart|intelligent|clever) as\b
bannedPhrases.why: The sheet concedes this: a Core runs a very good open-weight model, not the best model in the world this month. Never imply parity.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say "a capable model that is yours".

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(knows|remembers|reads|tracks|understands|sees) (everything|all)\b|\bnever forgets?\b|\breads your mind\b|\bpredicts? (your|what you)\b|\banticipat\w+\b|\bproactive(ly)?\b|\bnotices what you'?ve dropped\b|\bknows you better\b|\bperfect (recall|memory)\b
bannedPhrases.why: Proactive forecasting cards ("Your week, taking shape", "It notices what you've dropped") carry a Rolling out pill upstream. Today Companion Memory supplies individual context to OpenClaw and Hermes.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say what the agent was asked to do and what it pulled from Companion Memory.

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(books?|orders?|buys?|pays?|purchases?|negotiates?|cancels?|calls?|emails?|texts?|schedules?|files?|submits?)\b.{0,30}\b(for you|on your behalf|automatically|by itself|on its own|without (asking|you))\b
bannedPhrases.why: Agents act inside permissions the family sets. No story may show an agent spending money, contacting a third party or cancelling something without the person approving.
bannedPhrases.fix: Show the agent preparing the action and the person approving it.

bannedPhrases.why: OpenClaw and Hermes can be pointed at cloud model providers. A "private agent" scene is private only on the Core's local model; never show or mention a cloud key.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say the agent runs on the Core's local model.

bannedPhrases.why: Hermes reaches you through messengers that are someone else's servers. The message travels through them.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say the agent runs at home and the messenger is the messenger.

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(from anywhere|anywhere in the world|on the road|on holiday|while (you('| a)re |they('| a)re )?(away|travell?ing|out)|remote(ly)?( access)?|access (it|your \w+|your Core) (from|when|while)|away from home|from (your|the) (office|car|airport|hotel|train)|VPN|Tailscale|Cloudflare|tunnels?|public (URL|link|web|site)|share (a|the) link|reach(able)? (it )?(from|over) the (internet|web))\b
bannedPhrases.why: CAMPAIGN.md 13: remote access is NOT finalised ([x]). Docs describe Tailscale and Cloudflare, the sheet does not, and whether a relay or account is involved is unanswered. Keep every scene inside the home network.
bannedPhrases.fix: Set the scene at home, on the home Wi-Fi.

bannedPhrases.why: Mobile is closed preview; no store listing exists. In the FTUE the phone uses its browser/Wi-Fi settings only. (Third-party apps such as Immich have their own phone apps; do not show store badges.)
bannedPhrases.fix: Say "your phone".

bannedPhrases.why: Founder letter: "Multi-user operation is on the roadmap, but not on the box." Per-app multi-user (Immich, Nextcloud, Vaultwarden) is that app's feature; platform-level separation of one person's memory or agent from another's is not claimed. (CI-Docs says each person uses their own Companion account via Organizations; that conflicts, hold.)
bannedPhrases.fix: One household, one Core. Each person names and talks to their own agent; say nothing about isolation.

bannedPhrases.pattern: \bCompanion (Core|Hub|OS|Memory|Intelligence)\b[^.]{0,80}\b(open[- ]source|open source|source[- ]available|fully open|inspect(able)?|auditable|transparent code)\b|\b(open[- ]source|fully open|inspect(able)?|auditable)\b[^.]{0,60}\bCompanion (Core|Hub|OS|Memory)\b|\bopen the core\b|\beverything is inspectable\b
bannedPhrases.why: The open-source position is [x] unanswered (CAMPAIGN.md 16). No Companion component may be called open-source or inspectable until the component-by-component answer is published. The third-party apps in the catalogue may be called open-source (their manifests say so).
bannedPhrases.fix: Say the app is open source (if it is) or say nothing.

bannedPhrases.why: Owner ruling 22 Sep 2026: "Own outright" is retired. Users do not own the apps. "No API bill" is the accurate line. ("The AI That You Own" is the sanctioned tagline, used verbatim only.)
bannedPhrases.fix: Say your Core, your data, no API bill.

bannedPhrases.why: Steam Headless needs the family's own Valve account and a GPU the Core may not have; it streams inside the home network only (CAMPAIGN.md 13: no remote access claim). It is not a gaming PC or a console replacement, and it does not play anywhere or skip the Steam account.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say Steve plays his own Steam library, streamed from the Core to the screen in his room.

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(designed (and|&) (built|assembled|made)|designed in|built in (California|the USA|America)|made in (the )?(USA|America|California)|American[- ]made|handmade in|hand[- ]built|Silicon Valley (built|made))\b
bannedPhrases.why: Owner ruling 22 Sep 2026: only "Assembled, configured and burn-in tested in California; mainboards from Framework." "Designed" is nowhere on the sheet and country-of-origin wording is regulated.
bannedPhrases.fix: Use the ruled sentence.

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(never (crash|crashes|fail|fails|goes down|breaks?|needs? (updates|maintenance|attention))|always works?|100% uptime|zero downtime|maintenance[- ]free|zero maintenance|set it and forget it|fire and forget|runs forever|lasts forever)\b
bannedPhrases.why: Unmeasured reliability claims. The sheet says "without you babysitting it" and "walk away".
bannedPhrases.fix: Use the sheet's own phrases.

bannedPhrases.why: Never present covert or blanket recording of family members or guests. Companion Capture records the user's own machine; Frigate records the family's own cameras on their own property. Neither is for monitoring people who have not agreed.
bannedPhrases.fix: Show consent explicitly or leave it out.

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(testimonials?|customer stor(y|ies)|real (families|family|customers?|people|users)|actual (customers?|users|families)|our (customers|users|backers|families) (say|love|tell|report)|as seen (on|in)|rated|five[- ]stars?|\d(?:\.\d)? stars?|(?:customer|user|five[- ]star|\d+) reviews?|reviews? (?:from|by|say)|trusted by|used by (millions|thousands|hundreds|families)|\d+ (customers|users|families|backers|households)|case stud(y|ies)|success stor(y|ies)|before and after)\b
bannedPhrases.why: The families are fiction (see disclosures). Nothing may read as a testimonial, review, case study or usage count. CAMPAIGN.md 17: never present any person as a customer or team member.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say "story" or "scene" and keep the fictional disclosure in view.

bannedPhrases.why: No simulated capability. A scripted scene is not a recording. Only say "photograph" or "recording" for a real photograph or session on real hardware.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say "scene" or "drawing".

bannedPhrases.pattern: \b(render(ed|ing|s)?|3D model of the Core|photoreal\w*|product shot|hero shot)\b.{0,40}\b(Core|Companion Core)\b|\b(Core|Companion Core)\b.{0,40}\b(render(ed|ing|s)?|photoreal\w*|product shot)\b
bannedPhrases.why: Kickstarter forbids photoreal renders of the product. The Core is drawn stylised, line-drawing style, never as a finished-product render.
bannedPhrases.fix: Say "drawing".

bannedPhrases.why: A fictional address must not be a real person's address. A street number plus a real ZIP is exactly that. Use invented street names, no ZIP, or a place that cannot resolve.
bannedPhrases.fix: Invent a street; omit the ZIP.

bannedPhrases.why: Internal house ids, Sims-creator names and the ?house= URL form must not appear on any public surface, link or displayed string (old ?house=<id> keeps working but is never displayed or linked).
bannedPhrases.fix: Use the public family slug (/family/<slug>).

bannedPhrases.why: Ordinary words that are also internal house ids. Fine in prose; never in a URL, slug, file name, data attribute, og:image path or alt text that names the house.
bannedPhrases.fix: Check that the hit is prose, not an identifier.

requiredVocabulary.rule: Title Case. First mention per page/film is the full name; "your Core" or "the Core" after. Never home server, NAS, box (except the sanctioned "One box." line), appliance.
Title Case. The platform and the store: "the Companion Hub store" is the sheet's phrase. Never app store, marketplace, CI-Hub.
Title Case. Never Digital Memory, CI Memory, knowledge base, memory system.
Lower-case "account". The user-facing name for Portal / CI Account. Say it only if the owner settles the pairing question (see STORY-BIBLE 8).
Exact spelling. An agent. The sheet: "OpenClaw for browser automation". Attribute to the OpenClaw Foundation on credits. The catalogue lists the Companion edition as "OpenClaw WebCLI".
Exact spelling. An agent. The sheet: "Hermes for messaging". Attribute to Nous Research on credits.
The word for OpenClaw and Hermes. Never chatbot, bot, AI assistant, assistant.
Verb, lower-case in running text. The sign-off is exactly "UnCloud your life."
Allowed instead of "unlimited", only where the sheet supports it. "No API bill" is the sheet's accurate line.
With "available": "300+ apps and agents available in the Companion Hub store." is the only count.

allowedClaims.text: Your AI should answer to you.
Stop renting your intelligence.
allowedClaims.source: Owner approval, 2026-10-20 (lander spec decision D1 B); the exact line is not in CAMPAIGN.md or COPY.md
allowedClaims.note: The lander's H1 and the ad kit's last line (content/story/lander.json messages). Approved by the owner for use verbatim on 2026-10-20 (answered in the lander build session). It is the owner's wording, not a line of the campaign decks, so a change to it is the owner's to make here.

allowedClaims.text: UnCloud your life.
Companion Intelligence builds private, personal AI infrastructure for individuals, families and small teams who want powerful AI without cloud dependency.
allowedClaims.note: This sentence is what licenses a families-and-small-business site.

allowedClaims.text: Every cloud-based AI you use is someone else's agent. You are renting intelligence, and paying for it with the raw material of your life: your files, your correspondence, your half-finished ideas, your questions at 2am.
Core is the other option. A quiet, 24/7-ready machine, smaller than a sheet of paper, that holds local models in unified memory and answers only to the person in the room.
The intelligence that knows the most about you should live in your house.
allowedClaims.note: Adapted from the founder letter and awaiting owner sign-off in COPY.md 13.

allowedClaims.text: Plug it in, pair it over Wi-Fi, and walk away.
allowedClaims.note: The sheet's only setup sentence. See the FTUE table.

allowedClaims.text: Other agents are double agents. They serve a company whose interests are not yours, and they take your context with them. These do not.
allowedClaims.note: The sharpest line the company has. Use once, verbatim.

allowedClaims.text: A local machine does not run a frontier model. It runs a very good open-weight one. What a Core buys is a capable model that is yours: resident, private, and not subject to anyone else's roadmap.
allowedClaims.note: The honesty clause. It must appear once on the site.

allowedClaims.text: Companion Core is a 4.3 litre computer, about three quarters the footprint of a sheet of paper.
allowedClaims.source: CAMPAIGN.md 6 (232 x 205 x 90 mm, 4.3 L, 0.762 of a sheet)

allowedClaims.text: 19 dB at idle.
allowedClaims.note: Always "at idle". No load figure exists.

allowedClaims.text: Assembled, configured and burn-in tested in California, with mainboards from Framework.
Standard Mini-ITX hardware in a steel case, with two M.2 slots that stay yours. Memory is soldered and cannot be upgraded.
allowedClaims.note: Claim and limit travel together.

allowedClaims.text: Charcoal or Chalk.

In the box: Companion Core, assembled, burned in and tested; a power cable for your region; a quick-start guide with a warranty card; a Companion OS recovery USB; access to docs.ci.computer and the community.
allowedClaims.note: The unboxing scene may show exactly these objects and no others. The year of Hub Pro is a licence, not an object, and is left out of the story (campaign terms).

allowedClaims.text: Every machine ships with a drive fitted and Companion OS already on it.

forbiddenClaims.why: No dollar figure anywhere. See banned num-dollar.
No savings, payback, ROI or "replaces $X a month". No such figure exists in any app listing; 75% and 95% are marketing math; the sheet says about ten months, copy.json says about 26.
No Core tier, ship quarter, pledge, Early Bird, warranty, shipping or duty statement. The campaign page owns these.
No tok/s, latency, load noise, power draw, temperature, weight, certifications, PSU form factor, ROCm version, agent build number, benchmark score (Agentic Memory-System Benchmark).
No parity or superiority claim against cloud models.
No setup or install duration (minutes, hours).
No unhackable, guaranteed, end-to-end, bank-grade, nobody-can-see wording.
No "nothing ever leaves", "never phones home", "zero telemetry", "works offline", "air-gapped".
No HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA, SOC 2, PCI, certified, compliant, audited. A listing in the catalogue is not a compliance statement.
No medical, caregiving, safety-of-people or child-safety claim (eldercare, medication, parental control).
No legal validity of signatures, tax or financial advice, investment advice, "budget app saves you money".
Companion's own components are not yet declared open source. Third-party catalogue apps may be called open source.
"Own outright" retired; users do not own the apps.
Country-of-origin wording is regulated; only the ruled sentence.
Remote access is not finalised. No "from anywhere", VPN, tunnel, public link or "while you travel".
Mobile is closed preview. No Companion app, no store badges, no QR.
Platform multi-user is on the roadmap, not on the box. No per-person isolation of memory, agents or files.
Proactive forecasts and "it notices" features are rolling out upstream. No omniscient, predictive or proactive agent.
Box-to-box Asks, payments or entitlement nodes, OCR for scanned PDFs, app-declared intents, speculative inference are roadmap. Do not show them working. Import Tools and Companion Earth are retired.

Pendants and glasses (OMI, Mentra, Even Realities, MaixCAM, Pebble) feeding Companion Memory: the capture-to-memory chain is documented as broken at most joints. Companion Glasses Bridge is available:false. Do not draw or narrate wearables feeding the Core.
No agent spends money, contacts a third party or cancels a service without the person approving.
OpenClaw and Hermes can be pointed at cloud model providers. Never imply an agent is private if it is pointed at one; never show an API key.
A message sent through WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, SMS or email passes through that service. Hermes at home does not make the messenger local.
The families are fiction. No testimonial, review, case study, rating, user count, "real family".

No named real person, no founder photo or bio, no team photo. A founder name exists (Liam Broza) but no bio or photo may appear in a family story. Fictional characters must not share a name with a real, identifiable person at a real address.

No blanket recording of family members or guests. Cameras are the family's own, on their own property, with the household aware.
No unsourced factual allegation about a named company. Pair names only as the catalogue "replaces" table does.
Wrong product names: CI Account, Portal, CI Memory, Digital Memory, Companion Core Subscription, Core Subscription, Import Tools.

personaModel.status: Defined by r-facts. No user-facing agent persona exists in Companion Hub, the marketplace manifests or CI-Docs (see STORY-BIBLE 9).
rules: The family gives the agent a name; that is story, not a product setting. Never say Hub has a persona or personality setting.
poweredBy is one or more of ci-hermes (messaging), ci-openclaw (browser automation and tool use), plus ci-memory for context.
job is one sentence naming tasks the listed apps can really do. personality is three plain words, shown as tone of the caption, never as a capability.
Captions describe the agent in the third person ("Juniper files the school forms in Nextcloud"). If a quoted agent line is shown it is labelled scripted and is short.
No agent acts without the person approving anything that costs money or reaches a third party.
No persona claims to remember "everything". It pulls from Companion Memory what that person connected, opt-in.
One household, one Core. Do not suggest isolation between people.
